Cardiac: signs of heart failure S3, S4, gallops (thiamin, selenium deficiency, anemia, eating

Genito/urinary: delayed puberty (marasmus, eating or exercise disorder), hypogonadism

Back/Extremities: bone tenderness, kyphosis, edema (thiamin and protein deficiency), 
growth retardation, failure to thrive (energy deficiency), hyporeflexia (thiamin deficiency), 
kyphosis (osteoporosis), muscle wasting and weakness, bone pain (vitamin D, magnesium 
deficiency, marasmus), tenderness at end of long bones (vitamin D deficiency), squaring of 
shoulders-loss of deltoid muscles (kwashiorkor), diminished sensation to light touch (diabetes 
mellitus), kyphosis, scoliosis (osteoporosis).

body fat in some underweight people, such as the elderly who have lost lean tissue. 
However, consistent, accurate trended measurements of BMI provide important data 
regarding nutritional health. As such, inclusion of this measurement should be seen as 
routine in both ambulatory and institutional settings. Nurse Practitioners who deter-
mine patient numeracy regarding BMI can more effectively use this number as an 
outcome measure when developing treatment plans with their patients. Sharing trends 
in BMI with patients gives them additional data to reinforce the treatment plan.
